newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Goh says concerned about retail sector.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Goh says concerned about retail sector.

text.p: Prine Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Thursday the city state's economic slowdown was no cause for alarm, but expressed concerned about the slower pace of the retail sector.

"The current economic slowdown is no cause for alarm. It is due to a downturn in the global electronics cycle which then ripples through other sectors of the economy," he said in a speech for a Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce dinner.
But Goh said: "I am concerned, however, over the slower pace of retail business. The market has changed and there is an over-supply of retailers."
He said the government was in touch with key players in a number of industries and he was reassured to know many are optimistic of a turnaround by next year.
Singapore's export-led growth has slowed in recent months, with a sag in demand for electronic products a key factor.
Earlier this week the government said it was lowering its estimate of gross domestic product growth for 1996 to about six percent, from the previous seven to eight percent forecast.
Goh said many companies have said they would use the slowdown to restructure and reorganise, so that when the demand picks up again, they will be ready for it.

Turning to the retail sector, he said competition had increased with shoppers able to buy from more domestic outlets "and increasingly even overseas because of our strong dollar and Singaporeans' frequent travels abroad."
Goh said the government would help businesses, including the retail industry, restructure, and cited a variety of government programmes companies could take advantage of.

According to government figures, Singapore's main measure of retail sales declined 4.0 percent from a year earlier in August, the latest month for which figures have been released, and dropped 5.4 percent from July 1996.
